articleSummary: Urinary tract infection (UTI) symptoms and prevention in Thailand: UTIs are commonly caused by Escherichia coli and can ascend from the bladder to the kidneys. Treatment is usually antibiotics, with improvement in 2–3 days; complete the full course to prevent resistance. Recurrent UTIs may warrant low-dose preventive therapy; probiotics may help reduce long-term risk. If symptoms persist or worsen, further evaluation is advised to prevent kidney involvement. articleSummary: Chikungunya exposure in-utero in Brazil is linked to higher long-term morbidity. In a registry-based cohort of infants born 2015–2018, 1,821 exposed and 18,210 unexposed children were followed for all-cause first hospitalization or death up to age 3 years. Adjusted Cox models show a hospitalization hazard ratio of 1.21 (95% CI 1.11–1.36), translating to 37 excess hospitalizations per 1,000 exposed (95% CI 16–64). Intrapartum exposure yielded about a twofold risk (HR 2.08; 95% CI 1.33–3.44), with elevated risk also observed for first- and second-trimester exposure. Evidence for increased mortality was limited. The study demonstrates a persistent hospitalization risk associated with in-utero chikungunya exposure through early childhood in Brazil.

articleHeadlineTranslated: New recombinant mpox virus strain concerns the WHO.
articleHeadline: Nova cepa do vírus da mpox recombinante preocupa a OMS
articleSummary: New recombinant mpox (monkeypox) virus strain raises WHO concern. Detected February 2026, the novel recombinant blends genetic elements from mpox clade Ib (more severe, higher mortality, especially in children/immunocompromised) and clade IIb (driving the 2022 global outbreak). WHO suggests broader circulation than reported; two confirmed cases with travel histories—UK and India—signal transmission across at least four countries in three WHO regions. Conventional PCR failed to identify the recombinant; whole-genome sequencing confirmed the hybrid. Therapeutically, tecovirimat’s utility is questioned after the STOMP trial (344 immunocompetent adults with clade 2 mpox) showed no improvement in lesion resolution (83% vs 84%), pain reduction (0.1/10), or viral clearance; PALM007 in DRC with clade 1 yielded similar results, highlighting gaps for immunocompromised, pregnant, and pediatric patients. In Brazil, clade Ib detected in São Paulo (March 2025). Prevention centers on vaccination with Jynneos (MVA-BN) via SUS for priority groups, now emphasized.
notes: 記事サマリーで確認される主要発生地は南米（ブラジル・サンパウロ）とアジア（インド）。UK・DRCも言及されるが、対象国リストに含まれないため除外。新規組換え株（clade Ib × clade IIb）の出現は予想外。従来のPCRでは検出困難であり、ゲノムシーケンシング確認。tecovirimat有効性の課題（STOMP・PALM007試験でも改善なし）が治療面での懸念を加える。複数WHO地域での確認と旅行歴の存在により国際的拡大リスクが高い。

articleSummary: On 21 March 2026, An Giang Department of Health issued a press release about a meningococcal meningitis case in Phu Quoc Special Zone. Other students and teachers are under health monitoring; about 70 close contacts are monitored. Meningococcal disease (Group B) is respiratory-transmitted and can cause meningitis with 8-15% mortality and 10-20% neuro sequelae.

articleSummary: Pneumococcal disease and RSV infections are forecast to rise in early 2026 in Vietnam, especially among children and the elderly, per the Ministry of Health's 2026 Infectious Disease Prevention Plan. RSV affects the elderly and infants; CDC 2024–2025 data show 3.6–6.5 million outpatient visits, 190k–350k hospitalizations, 10k–23k deaths; Vietnam’s RSV infections are estimated at 4.5 million (2020–2025). Emphasis on early risk assessment and integrated prevention, with social mobilization per policy 282/NQ-CP.

articleHeadline: 'Gánh nặng kép' khi người già mắc bệnh mạn tính nhiễm khuẩn hô hấp
articleSummary: Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, 21 March 2026 — The annual respiratory conference warns of a 'double burden' of chronic bacterial respiratory infection among the elderly. Chronic conditions (cardiovascular disease, COPD, diabetes, immunodeficiency) raise risk of severe infection. Experts call for holistic, risk-based management and better translation of new evidence into practice, with Pfizer Vietnam support.

articleHeadline: Pneumococcus continues to be leading cause of community-acquired pneumonia
articleSummary: Pneumococcal disease (Streptococcus pneumoniae) remains a leading cause of community-acquired pneumonia in Viet Nam, with RSV also a major contributor to respiratory illness in children and older adults. At the Ho Chi Minh City Respiratory Society Annual Congress 2026 on March 21, experts highlighted a projected RSV burden in Viet Nam of nearly 4.5 million acute respiratory infections from 2020–2025, alongside international data (CDC Oct 2024–May 2025) estimating 3.6–6.5 million outpatient visits, 190,000–350,000 hospitalizations, and 10,000–23,000 deaths, with highest hospitalization in adults >75 and infants 0–11 months. Viet Nam faces rapid ageing, with 87.7% of older adults living with at least one chronic illness, creating a “double burden” on health systems. Discussions stressed early risk identification, prevention, and holistic respiratory care, plus stronger public-private collaboration; Pfizer Viet Nam served as scientific supporter.

articleSummary: Peru reports 1,045 leptospirosis cases and five deaths nationwide, per the Ministry of Health update (as of 2026-03-21). Of the fatalities, three are lab-confirmed and two are under investigation. The most affected areas are rainy regions, especially the Amazonas region and northern Peru; leptospirosis is endemic and occurs year-round, with a peak January–March during the rainy season. Flooding and pooled water, often mixing with sewage, raise exposure risk. Transmission occurs by contact of mucous membranes, eyes, or skin micro-lesions with contaminated water or animal urine. Leptospirosis is a zoonosis present in dogs, pigs, and rodents; outbreaks have been reported in military barracks due to rodent contamination of food. About 95 percent of patients recover without major issues; 5–10 percent may progress to Weil syndrome, with severity depending on multiple factors. Seek immediate health care for fever, headache, or calf pain and avoid entering flooded areas or wear rubber boots.

articleSummary: Harbin Institute of Technology surveyed 450 hepatitis B patients in China and identified six major commonalities driving chronic infection. Many carriers are asymptomatic and diagnosed only during routine exams, underscoring the silent nature of hepatitis B. A four-dimensional model is proposed: behavior exposure, immune status, lifestyle rhythm, and protective cognition. The six commonalities are: (1) frequent contact with incompletely sterilized invasive instruments during cosmetic or medical procedures; (2) sharing personal items such as razors, toothbrushes, or nail clippers; (3) long-term immune suppression from lifestyle stress; (4) poor vaccination awareness or failure to recheck anti-HBs antibody titers after vaccination; (5) irregular work–sleep cycles and high-fat, high-sugar diets that burden the liver; (6) cognitive biases about transmission, with underestimation of high-risk exposures and overestimation of safe social contact. Recommendations emphasize using regulated facilities, personal items, timely vaccination with antibody checks, regular liver screening, and health education.

In a survey of 1,108 orotracheal and cloacal swabs from 157 bird species, AIV RNA was detected in C. collaris using RT-qPCR targeting the matrix gene. Sequencing of the HA and NA genes showed 94% similarity to H5N2 strains previously identified in Colombian Anatidae in 2011, with other segments (NP; NS; PA; M; PB1; PB2) showing similarity to strains from both the American and Asian continents. This confirms the presence of a low-pathogenic H5N2 subtype in the Pantanal and suggests migratory birds play a key role in inland viral dissemination, while resident species may act as local reservoirs. No human cases reported; emphasizes routine AIV surveillance in South America as of 2026-03-22.

articleHeadline: 哈工大调查450名感染艾滋病人士，发现：患艾滋病的人，有4大共性_手机网易网
articleSummary: Harbin Institute of Technology surveyed 450 HIV-infected individuals across Chinese cities, revealing four recurring risk patterns. First, insufficient vigilance during the asymptomatic period, with long latent phases and potential transmission until CD4 counts drop below 200, presenting as recurrent oral ulcers, persistent low-grade fever, and unexplained weight loss. Second, misplaced trust in a single sexual encounter; many infections arise from unprotected one-time contacts, especially under alcohol or emotional pressure. Third, avoidance of HIV testing due to fear, delaying diagnosis; fourth, highly overlapping social networks and information silos, with outdated beliefs (AIDS stigma, “only certain groups risk it”) and low awareness of U=U. The study urges routine annual HIV screening for sexually active individuals, 4th-generation HIV testing at 2–4 weeks post-exposure with follow-up at 6 weeks, condom use reducing transmission by >90%, PEP within 72 hours, and strict ART adherence to achieve viral suppression and non-transmissibility.
notes: 記事は疫学調査の知見と予防啓発であり、感染症危機管理の対象シグナルではない。日常的なHIV啓発情報として分類される。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Scientists Alarmed: A Bat That Could Cause a New Epidemic Has Been Located.
articleHeadline: Cientistas alarmados: morcego que poderia causar uma nova epidemia foi localizado
articleSummary: Certain bat species do not present uniform spillover risk to humans. A Nature-published study maps viral lineages in bats and identifies groups with viral loads more compatible with human biology, marking them as higher priority for surveillance. The research shows that bats sharing physiological traits with primates are more likely to harbor viruses capable of infecting human cells without extensive mutations. Dense roosting colonies and this ecological context foster continuous viral circulation, effectively creating a natural lab for viral evolution. Molecular markers and non-invasive saliva and feces sampling enable monitoring of bats in tropical forests and rural areas. The focus includes bat families such as Pteropodidae, historically linked to past outbreaks. Habitat fragmentation drives contact with people as bats forage in orchards and crops near homes, elevating spillover risk to domestic animals or humans. Prevention hinges on ecosystem conservation, sustained genomic surveillance, and One Health approaches to reduce emergence.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Doctors warn after a death from meningococcal disease.
articleHeadline: Bác sĩ cảnh báo sau ca tử vong do não mô cầu
articleSummary: One death from meningococcal disease (Neisseria meningitidis) was reported in Phú Quốc on March 16, prompting parental concern over vaccination. Doctors warn against mass vaccination at crowded sites for children without high-risk factors, as such crowds may raise exposure to other respiratory infections. Meningococcal disease is an acute bacterial infection that can rapidly progress to septicemia or meningitis and is mainly transmitted via close respiratory contact; casual contact is unlikely to spread it. Early symptoms resemble ordinary respiratory illnesses—fever, sore throat, fatigue, headache—and the disease can quickly worsen to high fever, chills, vomiting, muscle/joint pain, and hypotension. A key warning sign is a petechial/purpuric rash that does not blanch, spreading rapidly and needing urgent care. The case involves a 10-year-old girl in Phú Quốc who died from meningococcal group B disease. Vaccination remains beneficial but should follow schedule or doctor guidance, with emphasis on hand hygiene, masking, ventilation, and avoiding close contact during outbreaks or after exposure.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Acre is among the states on alert for an increase in SARI, according to Fiocruz.
articleHeadline: Acre está entre os estados em alerta para aumento de SRAG, aponta Fiocruz
articleSummary: Acre is among 20 Brazilian states with SARI (Severe Acute Respiratory Infection) activity at alert/high risk per Fiocruz InfoGripe for Week 10 (Mar 8–14), ahead of autumn. Nationally, influenza A is rising before the peak season; RSV contributes to severe cases in children under 2 in Acre and other Northern states (Amazonas, Pará, Roraima, Rondônia). Rhinovirus drives pediatric hospitalizations; influenza A is the main cause of severe illness in young and older adults; Covid-19 persists at lower levels, concentrated in the Southeast. Brazil records 20,311 SARI cases in 2026, with 37% testing positive for a respiratory virus. Among positives: rhinovirus 41.9%, influenza A 21.8%, Covid-19 14.7%, RSV 13.4%, influenza B 1.5%; influenza A rose to 25.4% of positives in the last four weeks. Vaccination starts March 28: Nordeste/Centro-Oeste/Sul/Sudeste (Mar 28–May 30); Norte may vary. RSV vaccine for pregnant women; influenza A vaccination begins for priority groups on the 28th.
